Parturition is the formal, scientific word for the act of giving birth. It refers to the complete physical process by which a pregnant female — human or animal — delivers her offspring from her body. In everyday language, you might call this "childbirth," "labor and delivery," or simply "giving birth." In medicine, biology, and veterinary science, the single precise word for all of that is parturition.

Parturition is not just the final moment a baby is born. It refers to the entire process — from the very beginning, when the mother's body starts contracting and preparing to push the baby out, all the way through to the actual delivery of the offspring. Think of it as an umbrella term that covers everything happening during that event.

To put it simply: labor is part of parturition. Delivery is part of parturition. Parturition is the whole thing, start to finish.

This is one of the most important things to understand about this word: it applies to all mammals, not just humans. When a dog gives birth, that is parturition. When a horse, a cow, a whale, or a cat gives birth, that is also parturition. This is why scientists and veterinarians love this word — it is a single, clean, species-neutral term that works across all of biology. "Childbirth" only really fits humans. "Parturition" fits everyone.

You will mostly encounter this word in formal, professional, or academic settings:

  • Medical textbooks and research papers discussing pregnancy and delivery
  • Obstetrics (the branch of medicine dealing with pregnancy and birth)
  • Veterinary science, when discussing how animals deliver their young
  • Biology and zoology, when studying reproduction in mammals
  • Clinical notes written by doctors or midwives

You would almost never hear it in casual conversation. Nobody says, "She went through parturition on Tuesday." In daily life, people say "She gave birth" or "She had the baby." But the moment you step into a scientific or clinical context, parturition is the precise, preferred term.
How is it different from similar words?

These words all orbit the same event, but they are not identical:

  • Birth is the broadest and most general word — it can even be used metaphorically (e.g., "the birth of an idea"). It focuses on the outcome (a new life has arrived), not the process.
  • Childbirth is specific to humans and is the common everyday word for the same process. It is warm and familiar, not clinical.
  • Labor refers to only one phase of the process — the hard, muscular work the mother's body does (contractions) to push the baby toward delivery. Labor is a part of parturition.
  • Delivery refers to the final act — the moment the baby actually exits the body. Delivery is also a part of parturition.
  • Parturition is the scientific umbrella that covers the full process, applies to any species, and carries no emotional tone — it is neutral, precise, and formal.

• "The veterinarian stayed by the mare's side as parturition began."
  • "Hormonal changes in the weeks before parturition prepare the body for labor."
  • "Complications during parturition can pose serious risks to both mother and offspring."
  • "The researcher studied parturition across multiple mammal species to understand how birth timing differs."
  • "Parturition in elephants lasts longer and is more complex than in most other land mammals."

If you ever need to recall this word quickly: parturition = the scientific term for the complete process of giving birth, applicable to humans and animals alike.

That is the whole word — precise, formal, biological, and universal.
